UK and Germany strengthen defence ties in London talks
UK and Germany deepen defence-industrial cooperation at Lancaster House talks, building on the Trinity House Agreement and Kensington Treaty.
- UK and Germany strengthened defence-industrial cooperation at the latest talks at Lancaster House.
- The talks build on the Trinity House Agreement and Kensington Treaty, reinforcing cooperation between the two nations across air, land, sea and space.
- Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard and German counterpart State Secretary Jens Plötner joined industry leaders to discuss industrial priorities for collaboration.
UK-German work on key industrial collaboration and new technology was advanced yesterday as Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard hosted his German counterpart, State Secretary for Armament and Innovation Jens Plötner, at Lancaster House in London.
The latest UK-Germany Ministerial Group on Equipment and Capability Cooperation (MECC) meeting brought together senior officials and military leaders from both nations to review progress on joint defence capability programmes and to deepen the industrial partnership between the UK and Germany, two of NATO’s leading defence powers.
Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard MP said:
  Germany is one of our closest and most valued defence partners, and today’s talks demonstrate our determination to turn that ambition into real capability for our armed forces and real opportunity for our defence industries.
As threats to our shared security evolve, the UK and Germany are standing together, strengthening our forces, our industrial bases and our resilience in lockstep.
Discussions built on the Trinity House Agreement, signed in October 2024, which set out an ambitious programme of bilateral cooperation across air, land, maritime, cyber and space domains. The agreement sits under the wider Kensington Treaty, signed in July 2025, which provides the strategic framework for the UK-Germany relationship.
Among the flagship programmes on the agenda was Deep Precision Strike, a joint UK-Germany initiative to develop long-range strike capability, reflecting the shared ambition of both nations to address critical capability gaps and strengthen NATO’s deterrence.
The talks follow the Prime Minister’s visit to Berlin on 8 October, during which the UK and Germany agreed to deepen cooperation on space and to establish a new UK-Germany Counter-Hybrid Partnership, strengthening joint resilience against grey-zone threats.
Following the MECC meeting, Minister Pollard joined State Secretary Plötner at the German Embassy in London for a panel discussion which saw senior policymakers and industry leaders take stock of defence-industrial progress and identify practical priorities for deepening cooperation.
Minister Pollard was joined on the panel by State Secretary Plötner, Dr Philipp Kerth, co-founder and chief executive of German defence technology company Hypersonica, and Alex Zino, Director Business Development & Future Programmes at Rolls-Royce.
The MECC forms part of a wider programme of UK-German engagement in the lead-up to the EU-UK summit. The UK-Germany defence relationship continues to grow as both nations work towards a more resilient Euro-Atlantic security architecture, underpinned by a modern, innovative and competitive defence industrial base at the heart of NATO’s deterrence and readiness.

EU leaders rally around Zelenskiy as Trump calls Ukrainian strikes on Russia a 'disgrace'
BRUSSELS/KYIV, Oct 16 - European Union leaders rallied around President Volodymyr Zelenskiy at a summit on Friday as US President Donald Trump fired another salvo at Ukraine, calling its strikes on Russian refineries a "disgrace".
The EU is hosting Zelenskiy in Brussels at one of the most difficult moments for Ukraine, with missiles and drones raining down on Ukrainian cities and fears that the US could pull back intelligence sharing and weapons support from Kyiv.
Trump blindsided Zelenskiy last weekend by announcing that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other's energy facilities. Facing US midterm elections in November, Trump has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for pushing up energy prices that could cost him at the ballot box.
The US has also struck a diesel deal with Russia, angering Ukraine and European allies.
"We want to end this war as quick as possible. We don't see now signals from the Russian side that they are ready for this, to end this war. That's why we have to prepare for the winter," Zelenskiy said as he arrived at the summit, hugging many of the leaders as he met them.
"The winter package is not only energy, it's also air defence and funding," Zelenskiy said.
In the latest attacks, Russian drone strikes on the city of Kharkiv killed three people, while strikes elsewhere left hundreds of thousands of people without power.
In an interview, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal told Reuters that the EU would probably have to provide a new loan to Ukraine to help cover its budget gap for next year.
“Last winter was already hell, this one will be once again like hell,” Michal said.
"We have a lot of gaps to fill, and this is a European mission to fill the gaps that Ukraine needs. Because always, at the start (and) at the end of every conversation, people need to be reminded that we are sitting in a warm room, lights are on, heating is on, the coffee is warm, and we cannot get tired of the war in Ukraine, because they are fighting ... for us."
NO READY-MADE EUROPEAN ALTERNATIVE TO STARLINK
Ukraine's leadership has been alarmed by disruptions to the SpaceX Starshield satellite system used by Kyiv for battlefield communications and drone operations. A source in Ukraine's defence ministry said on Thursday that Starshield receptors were only working at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph), complicating their use for military missions.

Europe does not have a ready-made alternative to Starlink, although European governments and companies are working on long-term options.
"Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine. And unfortunately, in short term, Europe can't replace this capability," said the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas.
"We are working on the new sanctions package to put the pressure on Russia, and we of course hope that we do this with all our partners around the world," she added.
Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery after Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning the energy ceasefire that Trump had announced.
"All he's doing is making the world oil price higher. Well, I think that's a disgrace," Trump said in an interview with the Newsmax news outlet.
While EU leaders hit out at the US deal to buy Russian diesel, they are also grappling with how to tackle energy prices that have soared since the Iran war, exposing divisions between member states on day one of the summit on Thursday.
Zelenskiy told Reuters earlier this month that Ukraine had agreed a plan with European partners that would allow it to close a $27 billion deficit in its military spending for this year, allowing it to order the drones needed to continue fighting at the start of 2027.
However, Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko said recently Ukraine still faced an unfunded budget gap for next year of $32.6 billion – and that does not include an estimated $40 billion in direct military supplies from allies.
"I am unhappy with the number of countries that have been willing to pledge new financial support to Ukraine," said Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten.
Sounding a more sceptical note, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker urged caution in the debate over making new, far-reaching financial commitments to Ukraine.
"There are so many figures being bandied about that we now need to put them into context, explain them and make it clear where this shortfall is coming from. I’m surprised too," he said. REUTERS

According to IRNA from the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, Seyyed Mohammad Atabak, on Wednesday evening, at the signing of the memorandum with the member states of the Eurasian Economic Union during the second meeting of the Joint Committee for the Implementation of the Free Trade Agreement between Iran and this union, called for operational follow-up of the agreements, the removal of trade barriers, and maximum use of the capacities of this agreement to develop economic exchanges.

The Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade stated: The negotiations held will be constructive and result-oriented, and the summary of the negotiations and approvals in specialized committees should be the basis for regular follow-up of commitments.
He expressed hope that the implementation of the agreements, while facilitating the activity of traders and increasing trade exchanges, would lead to strengthening economic cooperation between Iran and the Eurasian Economic Union and enhancing the position of the parties in regional and international relations.
The second meeting of the Joint Committee for the Implementation of the Free Trade Agreement between Iran and the Eurasian Economic Union was held, hosted by the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, with the presentation of solutions for trade facilitation, the development of economic cooperation, and the removal of existing barriers.
In this committee, the minister responsible for trade of the Eurasian Economic Union, officials of the Economic Commission, ambassadors, deputy ministers of the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, representatives of the Iran Trade Promotion Organization, the Customs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture, the Ministries Transport and Urban Development and Agriculture, and the National Standards Organization of Iran and the Iran Veterinary Organization were present.
Accelerating the establishment of the electronic system for verification of origin, developing transit cooperation within the framework of the International North–South Corridor, and strengthening technical and health cooperation related to trade were among the most important axes of this meeting.
Also, the signing of the cooperation memorandum of understanding between the Business Council of the Eurasian Economic Union and the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture was assessed as a step toward strengthening communication among private sector actors and expanding trade cooperation between the two sides.

Also, in mid-September, Iran’s Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance, offering a positive assessment of the results of his Tuesday meetings with officials of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), announced the proposal of initiatives such as setting a base currency to accelerate transactions and appointing special representatives to resolve obstacles facing bilateral trade.
According to IRNA, Seyyed Ali Madanizadeh, speaking to reporters after separate meetings and talks with the Chairman of the Executive Board and the Minister of Trade of the Eurasian Economic Commission at the union's headquarters in Moscow, added: "We held very good sessions."
He stated: "On Iran's behalf, we expressed our interest and readiness to expand relations and fully implement the free trade agreement with the Eurasian Economic Union, and that we are prepared to cooperate with this union in various fields; the union's officials, in turn, expressed their willingness and interest in expanding ties with our country."
The Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance, referring to the efforts of the enemies of the Iranian nation to fuel economic warfare and block trade and financial channels, said: "What is evident is that, thanks to God, these countries support Iran and our economy, and that Iran has managed to maintain production and trade relations with countries under the toughest conditions." He added: "The member states of the Eurasian Economic Union are equally committed and eager to develop these relations."
Continuing his Moscow visit agenda for multilateral consultations, the Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance attended the Eurasian Economic Union's headquarters and met with the Chairman of the Executive Board and the Minister of Trade to discuss accelerating bilateral trade.
Seyyed Ali Madanizadeh, and Bakytzhan Sagintayev, Chairman of the Board of the Eurasian Economic Commission, emphasized their shared determination to expand cooperation during this meeting.
Prior to this meeting, the Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance held a separate session with Andrey Slepnev, Minister in charge of Trade of the Eurasian Economic Commission, and a group of union officials to review the progress of cooperation following the implementation of the free trade agreement. Slepnev, noting that the second meeting of the Iran-EAEU working group would be hosted by Tehran in the coming months, expressed hope that the upward trend in bilateral trade would continue.
Iran's Ambassador to Russia, Kazem Jalali, and Mehdi Heydari, Deputy Minister of Economy and head of Iran's Organization for Investment, Economic and Technical Assistance, accompanied Madanizadeh during these meetings.
The free trade agreement between Iran and the Eurasian Economic Union came into force in May 2025 after completing legal procedures in the signatory countries, subsequently eliminating customs duties on 87% of goods in bilateral trade.
Within this cooperation framework, the path has been smoothed for Iranian goods to enter the market of over 180 million people in the union's member states, and reciprocally, this opportunity is available for traders from the five signatory countries in commerce with Iran.
Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Armenia are members of the Eurasian Economic Union, and Iran holds observer status in the union.
The Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) is a regional economic integration bloc in the post-Soviet space, established by a treaty signed in 2014 and launched on January 1, 2015. Its five member states are Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Armenia, with Iran, Cuba, Moldova, and Uzbekistan holding observer status.
Modelled in part on the European Union, the EAEU aims to create a single internal market with the free movement of goods, services, capital, and labour. Its core objectives include improving living standards, ensuring sustainable economic development, and boosting the global competitiveness of member economies.
The bloc is driven by institutions such as the Supreme Eurasian Economic Council and the Eurasian Economic Commission. While the EAEU has expanded external ties—notably through a free trade agreement with Iran—internal integration remains uneven, with Russia dominating trade flows in a "hub and spoke" model. The bloc has set a long-term vision to become a self-sufficient and attractive macro-region by 2045.

University's satellite collects data on space radiation at various heights above Arctic
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:46:24 UTC
16:46:24 KST

ARKHANGELSK, October 16. /TASS/. The ArcticSat-1 spacecraft of the Northern Arctic Federal University (NArFU) collected data on space radiation at different heights above the Arctic. Researchers obtained data from 500 to 200 km, and there is practically no information about radiation at low levels in the circumpolar regions, leader of the university's Space Monitoring Center Roman Alyoshko told TASS.
"The main data that we were collecting is data on space radiation," he said. "This is an urgent task exactly for the polar regions. During the spacecraft's mission, we collected data on space radiation, starting from altitudes of about 500 km when it was launched into orbit, and then it was gradually decreasing over about a year and a half, to 200 km when it already began burning up. And it is even more relevant data when it was in low orbits of about 200 kilometers. There are practically no spacecraft in such orbits, and therefore data on space radiation at these heights is very valuable."
ArcticSat-1 belongs to a group of satellites that fly in low orbits, at an altitude of 400-600 km. Strictly speaking, there is no space vacuum there, and therefore the satellite constantly touches the atmosphere molecules and gradually loses speed. It does not have an engine to compensate for this, so the satellite is slowly descending. The lower is the satellite, the denser is the air and the faster is the deceleration. The Sun also affects the descent rate: with high solar activity, the atmosphere heats up and "swells", increasing the braking effect at the orbit altitude.
ArcticSat-1's orbit is polar, with an inclination of about 97 degrees. In such an orbit, the spacecraft passes over high latitudes, where the geomagnetic field does not protect well from space particles. This coincides with the project's main topic: the impact of space weather on small spacecraft in the polar regions.
"We have focused on how this affects satellites. We were receiving data on space radiation and at the same time we were receiving information about the satellite. Our goal is to make recommendations for operators of such satellites on what to do in a certain situation. In case of a very strong surge of space radiation, it may be reasonable to put the satellite into the sleep mode, that is, not to interact with it - not to cause breakdowns," the scientist said, adding it was important to find how to "prolong the life" of such satellites.
An octopus in space
On board the satellite was an art object, an octopus, - Octo-Pax by artist Nastya Miro. This is a figurine of about ten by ten centimeters, made of a domestic metal powder composition. It was in a separate cube chamber inside the satellite. Inside the chamber was also a camera facing the art object.
The octopus, according to calculations, burned down along with the satellite. The art object ended the journey the way the artist had intended it to happen: it did not stay in orbit. Entering the atmosphere, the figure traveled the same path as the spacecraft. "This fate fits deeply the project's idea. Octo-Pax was holding in its tentacles debris that is common for the orbit, and symbolized the space's cleanup from debris. The art object did not become part of this debris, as it dissolved into the atmosphere, without leaving anything behind over there - outside the Earth," the university said.
The ArcticSat-1 satellite burned down in dense layers of the atmosphere. It had worked in orbit for about a year and a half. Scientists will be processing the data obtained by it for about a year.

porsche mission S reinterprets the sports car with cues from its racing heritage
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:45:21 UTC
16:45:21 KST

porsche mission S reinterprets the sports car with cues from its racing heritage
drawing on the 550 spyder, 911, and GT1, the vision model proposes a future for porsche that looks to its motorsport heritage, questioning the growing dominance of screens inside the car.
prefer designboom on google
[FEATURED]
a new sports car shaped by Porsche’s historic models
Porsche unveils the Mission S, a mid-engined super sports car vision model that reinterprets its design identity by drawing on historic racing automobiles while featuring a deliberately restrained digital interior. Developed by Style Porsche under Vice President Tobias Sühlmann, the concept forms part of the brand’s Sportwagenschmiede ‘35 strategic realignment and offers an early indication of the design direction Porsche intends to carry into future models. The project places particular emphasis on the relationship between driver and machine, retaining physical controls and familiar instruments. The Mission S points toward a potential expansion of Porsche’s sports car range. According to Chairman of the Executive Board Dr. Michael Leiters, the company is considering a permanent mid-engined super sports car positioned above the 911.
mission S points to a new chapter
The Mission S makes its connection to Porsche’s past through its proportions and individual design details. Its mid-engined architecture creates a low front end, prominent fenders, and the characteristic roofline that Porsche describes as a ‘flyline’. These elements establish the silhouette of the car, while a continuous line connecting the front and rear lighting gives the exterior a more unified appearance. The round headlights and pronounced fenders recall the 911, while the treatment of the bodywork’s shut lines references the G-model generation. The low front takes cues from the GT1, and the roofline extending toward the rear wing evokes the 959. At the back, a ‘car-in-car’ concept also draws on the GT1, translating an earlier racing design into a contemporary form.
The wheels reinterpret the dial-like pattern associated with the 928, with a new design intended to emphasize lightweight construction. Other functional details include a cooling solution inspired by the Porsche 917’s radiator fan and an integrated active rear wing. Together, these features present the Mission S as an exercise in adapting recognizable design references to a new vehicle architecture. Porsche describes the forms as ‘floating volumes’, with surfaces that appear to sit above the car’s underlying technical structure. A main horizontal line separates the more sculptural upper bodywork from the lower sections, where functional elements become more visible. This division gives the concept a visual language that balances muscular proportions with a relatively clean exterior.
the interior puts physical interaction back in focus
Porsche draws on the interiors of the 550 Spyder and 356, using two defining lines that extend across the dashboard and doors to establish a continuous visual relationship between the cabin and exterior. The instrument cluster combines five circular gauges with digital information. At its center, a rev counter uses an analogue needle with a display behind it. Depending on the selected driving mode, the arrangement of the instruments changes, with their housings positioned alongside one another or staggered to adjust the driver’s view. The concept also incorporates a reworked Sport Chrono element and push-pull controls for selected comfort and driving functions.
Instead of a built-in central screen or a passenger display, the Mission S has a retractable smartphone holder compatible with MagSafe. The phone can be used for navigation and other information, while the My Porsche App gives access to the car’s functions and different designs for the digital instruments. The setup keeps the dashboard simple, combining digital features with physical controls and a focus on driving.
a historical reference point for a future design identity
Porsche unveiled the Mission S on a pier in Queens, New York, the same location where photographs of the mid-engined 550 Spyder were taken in 1953. The setting connects the new concept to the company’s history and its early sports cars. The car’s white, gray, and red color scheme also references Porsche’s racing heritage. Special finishes, including Firn White Metallic and Light Red Metallic, are combined with Black Chrome and Special Black details. Porsche describes its future design direction through three principles: ‘authentic, consequent and timeless’. The Mission S brings together design elements from historic models with a new approach to the car’s proportions and interior.
For now, the Mission S remains a vision model, with no confirmed production plans. It offers an early look at how Porsche intends to develop its sports cars while retaining the design features and driving experience associated with the brand.

design: Style Porsche, Tobias Sühlmann, Vice President Style Porsche

Carnival Cruises axes half of Australian fleet
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:38:12 UTC
16:38:12 KST

In short:
Carnival Cruises will drop two of the four cruise ships in its Australian fleet.
All other major cruise lines have pulled their full-time Australian ships.
Australia is a hard market for cruises to stay profitable, according to an industry expert.
Carnival Cruises has announced it will remove two of its four Australian cruise ships from March 2028, despite more than 1.4 million Australians going on a cruise last year.
Carnival, which is the only major cruise company operating full-time in Australia, announced it was pulling the Carnival Adventure and the Carnival Luminosa.
Other major cruise operators such as Disney and Royal Caribbean no longer operate full-time in Australia.
Carnival said ship schedules were considered years in advance and it was considering "long-term certainty and globally competitive operating conditions to support itinerary planning and investment".
The decision was an economic one, according to Chris Frame, a maritime historian.
"Australia is an end-of-the-line destination, and it's a huge investment."
Mr Frame said higher levels of regulation, such as tough biosecurity rules, and little cruise infrastructure made it hard for cruises to stay profitable in Australia.
"Berthing fees are higher than other markets, refuelling is higher and provisioning the ship with food is higher, as you just don't have the economies of scale."
He said that for the company, the ships were assets and "they can always be redeployed somewhere else more profitable".
New changes to cruise laws
The moves comes after a decades-old temporary exemption, allowing cruise ships to circumvent Australian labour laws, was extended earlier this month, but with new protections added for workers for the first time.
Earlier this year, an ABC News investigation revealed that workers had accused the company of 12-hour work days for seven days a week, medical neglect, not providing safe drinking water and wages less than $3 an hour. Carnival denied the allegations.
Carnival's country manager Peter Little said in a statement the company had "greater exposure to changes in local market and operating conditions" than other cruise lines. Carnival did not respond to requests for comment.
However, Jake Field of the Maritime Union of Australia claimed this was the third time Carnival had threatened to withdraw from Australia, and that it was a negotiating tactic.
"There are 80 cruise vessels that are scheduled to come to Australia, only four of them don't have collective agreements with their crews, and those are the four Carnival ships," he said.
"We'll still be surrounded by water, and be an international cruise destination. Those 80 other cruise ships will still be coming here."

South Korea reviewing plan to expand Gulf operations, deploy additional maritime patrol aircraft: Report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:37:50 UTC
16:37:50 KST

Saadet Gokce
16 October 2026•Update: 16 October 2026
South Korea is reviewing plans to expand the operational area of one of its naval units operating around Somalia to the Gulf of Oman and deploy an additional maritime patrol aircraft amid increased shipping concerns, JoongAng daily reported Friday.
The Cheonghae Unit has operated in the Gulf of Aden off Somalia since 2009, escorting South Korean vessels and protecting them from piracy.
The proposed expansion would require adding a clause to the unit's deployment consent motion to cover other waters during emergencies involving South Korean nationals.
The government is also considering deploying a long-range maritime surveillance aircraft, potentially a P-8A Poseidon.
The Cheonghae Unit currently consists of one 4,400-ton-class destroyer, one maritime operations helicopter, up to three rigid-hull inflatable boats, and up to 320 service members.
South Korea’s Defense Ministry denied that the review to expand the unit's operational range was a response to a US request for troop deployment, saying it was considering submitting an extension motion before the current deployment authorization expires. It added that no details had been finalized.
There was no immediate official confirmation from Seoul on the issue.
The Gulf of Oman links the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Sea.
The discussions come as Seoul weighs possible contributions to efforts to ensure safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz amid pressure from Washington.
The Strait of Hormuz is a crucial energy corridor for South Korea, while the conflict involving Iran and increased activity by Yemen’s Houthi group around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait have raised concerns over shipping and crude supplies.

Three police officers in Dnipropetrovsk region suspected of armed robbery involving gunfire for $68,000
Kyiv • UNN
In Dnipropetrovsk region, three police officers are suspected of attacking a man and seizing cryptocurrency and cash worth more than $68,000. All of them were remanded in custody with bail set at UAH 3 million each.
In the Dnipropetrovsk region, three police officers are suspected of a robbery attack on a resident of Nikopol, during which they seized his cryptocurrency and cash worth more than $68,000. The court ordered pretrial detention for all the suspects. This was reported by the Office of the Prosecutor General, UNN writes.
Under the procedural guidance of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Prosecutor's Office, three police officers were notified of suspicion of a robbery attack on a resident of Nikopol. According to the investigation, they seized his cryptocurrency and cash worth a total of more than $68,000
The suspects include the deputy head of one of the police departments, the deputy head of the Department for Combating Drug-Related Crime of the regional Main Directorate of the National Police, and an operative of that department.
According to the investigation, the police officers learned that the man possessed a substantial amount of cryptocurrency and decided to take his money.
On the night of June 18, 2026, two of the suspects attacked him in the middle of the street, while the third coordinated their actions. They knocked the victim to the ground, used tear gas, fired several shots at him with a traumatic weapon, handcuffed him, and beat him.
Threatening him with a pistol, the attackers forced the man to transfer cryptocurrency worth $51,000 to a prepared wallet. After that, he was supposed to call his mother and demand that she hand over all the family's savings. Fearing for her son's life, the woman gave them more than $17,000.
After taking the money, the suspects threatened to kill the man if he contacted the police or a hospital. According to the investigation, they divided the money among themselves
The police officers' actions were classified under Part 4 of Article 187 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine — robbery committed by a group of persons acting pursuant to a prior conspiracy during martial law. On October 14, the court ordered pretrial detention for all three, with the right to post bail — UAH 3 million for each.
The pretrial investigation is ongoing. Other individuals who may have been involved in the crime are being identified.

US missile defence shortages could last until 2030, ousted general warned: report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:36:45 UTC
16:36:45 KST

Ousted US Army Chief of Staff General Randy George warned months before the US-Israeli war against Iran that American missile defence stockpiles were critically low and could take until 2030 to recover, CBS News reported on Thursday, citing US officials familiar with his assessment.
George raised the warning in late December, two months before the conflict began. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed him from his post in April as the war was under way.
The assessment, included in the Pentagon’s fiscal 2027 force allocation planning, identified shortages of Terminal High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) interceptors and Patriot missiles, with supplies expected to remain at strategically low levels until 2030.
Officials attributed the shortfall to weapons transfers to Ukraine, US military support for Israel and limited defence industry production capacity, according to the report.
War further strains supplies
The conflict with Iran has added pressure on US stockpiles. A Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimate found that US forces entered 2026 with about 2,300 Patriot interceptors and used between 1,050 and 1,430 of them during the conflict.
The US had about 355 THAAD interceptors before the war, of which an estimated 190 to 290 were expended, according to the estimates.
Mark Cancian, a retired Marine colonel and senior adviser at CSIS, told CBS News that the systems would be crucial in a potential conflict with China.
“Air defence, missile defence, that will be huge,” he said, explaining that a major confrontation with Beijing would require substantial interceptor supplies.
Replenishing the stockpiles could take years. CSIS estimates that new THAAD interceptor contracts take more than four years to fulfil, while Patriot PAC-3 orders take an average of three and a half years.
Pentagon denies shortage
The Pentagon rejected claims that US forces face a shortage of munitions.
“Claims of US munitions shortages are false,” chief spokesperson Sean Parnell told CBS News.
He added that Washington retained “everything required to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing”.

Russian defenses down 644 drones overnight, civilian injured in Rostov Region

MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Air defenses shot down 644 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, the Defense Ministry said in a statement.
A civilian was injured in the Rostov Region, where falling drone debris also damaged production and storage facilities.
TASS has gathered the key information about the consequences of the attacks.
Scale of attacks
- On-duty air defenses intercepted and destroyed 644 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles over Russian regions from 8:00 p.m. Moscow time on October 15 to 8:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 16 (5:00 p.m. - 5:00 a.m. GMT), the Defense Ministry said.
- According to the ministry, the drones were shot down over the Bryansk, Vologda, Volgograd, Voronezh, Vladimir, Kaluga, Kursk, Lipetsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Novgorod, Orenburg, Oryol, Pskov, Rostov, Ryazan, Samara, Saratov, Smolensk, Tambov, Tver, Tula, Ulyanovsk, Moscow, Leningrad, Krasnodar and Tatarstan regions, as well as Crimea and the Black Sea.
- Air defenses downed another 15 drones heading for Moscow, Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said on the Max social media platform.
- Earlier, Sobyanin said that 37 drones had been shot down shortly before midnight.
- A total of 57 drones flying toward Moscow have been shot down since midnight, according to TASS calculations based on data from Sobyanin.
- About 50 UAVs and projectiles were destroyed in Russia’s southern Rostov Region overnight, Governor Yury Slyusar said.
- According to him the city of Bataisk and nine districts came under attack.
- Air defenses shot down 27 Ukrainian drones over the central Kaluga Region, Governor Vladislav Shapsha wrote on Max.
- Another 15 Ukrainian drones were downed over the central Tula Region, Governor Dmitry Milyayev said.
- Earlier, he said that ten UAVs had been destroyed.
- Air defenses downed 12 Ukrainian drones over the western Smolensk Region last night, Governor Vasily Anokhin said.
- Ten Ukrainian UAVs were destroyed over the Voronezh Region in southwestern Russia, Governor Alexander Gusev wrote on Max.
- Eight drones were shot down over the central Yaroslavl Region, Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said on Max.
- An attack involving three drones was repelled in the northwestern Novgorod Region, Governor Alexander Dronov said.
Consequences
- A man was injured in a drone strike in the Aksaisky District of the Rostov Region, Governor Slyusar said.
- The man has been taken to the hospital.
- Falling drone debris damaged production and storage facilities in the Aksaisky District.
- A fire broke out but it has now been extinguished.
- The windows of two private houses were damaged in the Kuibyshevsky District.
- There were no casualties.
- Falling drone fragments damaged several windows and balconies in an apartment building, as well as a car, in a municipality in the Voronezh Region, Governor Gusev said.
- The windows of three private houses were damaged in another municipality.
- Emergency response teams are working at the sites where drone debris fell.
- The central Vladimir Region came under attack overnight, including an attempted strike on heating infrastructure in the regional capital, Governor Alexander Avdeyev said.
- According to him, minor damage was reported but there were no casualties.

Private healthcare providers back proposed rules to make fees more transparent
New rules could apply from August next year, requiring bilingual price lists, budget estimates and explanations for bills at least 20 per cent higher
Private hospitals and clinics have thrown their support behind proposed Hong Kong government measures that will make their pricing more transparent, such as publishing annual billing statistics, despite potentially higher operating costs.
Healthcare providers said on Friday that the latest proposed measures, which could start with private hospitals from August next year at the earliest, were “feasible” and “reasonable”.
Details were set out in a document submitted by the Health Bureau to the Legislative Council on Thursday evening, after the proposal was first floated in May last year.
The measures will cover price information, budget estimates and billing statistics.

Deutsch-Französische Einigung zu „Made in Europe“ und Autoabgasen verzögert sich – SPD erhebt Einwände
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:35:00 UTC
16:35:00 KST

Deutsch-Französische Einigung zu „Made in Europe“ und Autoabgasen verzögert sich – SPD erhebt Einwände
Der Vertragsentwurf sieht strengere Zulassungsbedingungen für Nicht-EU-Länder hinsichtlich der Teilnahme an öffentlichen Ausschreibungen und der Inanspruchnahme öffentlicher Fördermittel vor und mildert das Verbot von Verbrennungsmotoren ab dem Jahr 2035 ab.
Der französische Präsident Emmanuel Macron auf dem internationalen Pariser Autosalon an der Porte de Versailles in Paris am 12. Oktober 2026. | Poolfoto von Thibault Camus/AFP via Getty Images
BRÜSSEL — Frankreich und Deutschland konnten sich am Donnerstag nicht auf einen gemeinsamen Standpunkt zum Geltungsbereich der künftigen „Made in Europe“-Vorschriften der Union sowie zu größerer Flexibilität bei der Reduzierung der CO2-Emissionen und zum Verbot von Verbrennungsmotoren ab 2035 einigen.
Der Entwurf des Gegenseitigkeitsabkommens, über den POLITICO erstmals im Juli berichtet hatte, stellt eine bedeutende Annäherung zwischen den beiden Ländern dar und sollte eigentlich in Kürze unterzeichnet werden. Am Donnerstagabend geriet das Abkommen jedoch ins Stocken, da der Koalitionspartner SPD Einwände erhob. Befürchtet wurde, dass wichtige Umweltziele gestrichen worden seien.
„Eine endgültige Einigung steht noch aus“, erklärte ein Sprecher der deutschen Bundesregierung.
Advertisement
Anfang dieser Woche hatte der französische Präsident Emmanuel Macron angedeutet, dass nun Deutschland am Zug sei. „Auf der anderen Seite des Rheins gibt es politische Zwänge, und ich respektiere die Koalitionsgespräche voll und ganz“, sagte Macron am Montag am Rande des Pariser Autosalons.
Gemäß den Bedingungen des vorgeschlagenen Abkommens würde Deutschland strengere „Made in Europe“-Kriterien für den Automobilsektor im „Industrial Accelerator Act“ akzeptieren, auf die Frankreich gedrängt hat, im Gegenzug für eine Abschwächung des Verbots von Verbrennungsmotoren, einer der langfristigen Forderungen Berlins.
„Angesichts der erheblichen technologischen, wirtschaftlichen und geopolitischen Veränderungen seit der Einführung des bestehenden Rechtsrahmens sollte das Automobilpaket ein besseres Gleichgewicht zwischen Klimazielen, industrieller Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, technologischer Entwicklung und der Stärkung der europäischen Wertschöpfung herstellen“, schrieben die beiden Länder in einem POLITICO vorliegenden Vertragsentwurf.
„Auf der Grundlage der deutsch-französischen Ministerräte in den Jahren 2025 und 2026 schlagen Deutschland und Frankreich daher ein ausgewogenes Verhandlungspaket vor, das ehrgeizige CO2-Reduktionsziele mit zusätzlicher Flexibilität und gezielten Anreizen für die europäische Wertschöpfung verbindet“, heißt es in der Vereinbarung weiter.
Derzeit sieht das Ziel der EU vor, dass Unternehmen die Emissionen von Verbrennungsmotoren bis 2035 um 100 Prozent gegenüber dem Niveau von 2021 senken, wobei sie die Möglichkeit haben, sich durch Initiativen wie Ausgleichsmaßnahmen und Investitionen einen Spielraum von 10 Prozent bei den Emissionen zu „erwerben“.
Im Rahmen des vorgeschlagenen Abkommens wollen Frankreich und Deutschland das Ziel für 2035 auf 90 Prozent absenken und im Gegenzug für Investitionen in alternative Kraftstoffe einen zusätzlichen Spielraum von 10 Prozent einräumen (was insgesamt 80 Prozent ergibt).
Advertisement
Entscheidend für die Stahlhersteller und die linke SPD in Deutschland wäre, dass das deutsch-französische Abkommen die Investitionspflicht für „grünen Stahl“ abschaffen und damit einen wichtigen Anreiz beseitigen würde.
„Das zerstört den Leitmarkt für die Stahlindustrie“, erklärte ein Lobbyist der Branche gegenüber POLITICO unter der Bedingung der Anonymität, um über dieses heikle Thema sprechen zu können. Da der Vertragsentwurf keinen Druck auf die Automobilhersteller ausübe, „grünen Stahl“ zu beziehen, werde dieser dadurch zu einem „nice-to-have“-Extra, erklärte die Person.
Als Zugeständnis an Berlin wird im Vertragsentwurf betont, dass der sogenannte „Utility-Faktor“ – mit dem die Emissionen von Plug-in-Hybridfahrzeugen anhand des Verhältnisses zwischen der Nutzungshäufigkeit des Elektromotors und des Verbrennungsmotors berechnet wird – auf der Grundlage von Laborergebnissen und nicht, wie von der Kommission gefordert, anhand von Daten aus dem realen Fahrbetrieb ermittelt werden sollte. Diese Änderung wird den Automobilherstellern helfen, mehr Plug-in-Hybride zu verkaufen und gleichzeitig die übergeordneten Emissionsziele zu erreichen.
Als Gegenleistung für diese Emissionszugeständnisse schloss sich Deutschland der Forderung Frankreichs an, den Geltungsbereich der „Made in Europe“-Regelungen im Rahmen des „Industrial Accelerator Act“ der EU in Bezug auf den Automobilsektor einzuschränken.
Der Text gilt nur für die 27 EU-Mitgliedstaaten und wird unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen auf das Vereinigte Königreich ausgeweitet.
Der EU-Industriekommissar Stéphane Séjourné erklärte am Dienstag gegenüber POLITICO, er unterstütze das Abkommen als Weg aus der Sackgasse, und fügte hinzu, dass das Vereinigte Königreich derzeit die Voraussetzungen für das Label „Made in Europe“ erfülle.
Advertisement
Die Vereinbarung könnte den Stillstand sowohl bei der CO₂-Verordnung als auch beim IAA beenden, bei denen Frankreich und Deutschland bisher auf gegensätzlichen Seiten standen. „Die Bestandteile dieses Gesamtpakets sollten so schnell wie möglich und gleichzeitig verabschiedet werden“, schrieben die beiden Länder.
Die britische Regierung begrüßte die mögliche Einbeziehung des Vereinigten Königreichs in die „Made in Europe“-Vorschriften für Kraftfahrzeuge.
„Dies ist ein deutsch-französischer Vorschlag, und es muss noch ein europäischer Prozess durchlaufen werden, aber sollte er bestätigt werden, begrüßen wir das Ziel, das Vereinigte Königreich in den ‚Industrial Accelerator Act‘ einzubeziehen – das wäre eine gute Nachricht für die britische Automobilindustrie sowie für die Arbeitsplätze und Investitionen, die sie im gesamten Vereinigten Königreich sichert“, erklärte ein Sprecher von Downing Street Nr. 10 in einer Stellungnahme.
Sollte der deutsch-französische Deal unterschrieben werden, muss es noch von den anderen EU-Mitgliedstaaten und vom Europäischen Parlament gebilligt werden, die derzeit über das „Industrial Accelerator Act“ und das Automobilpaket, einschließlich der Emissionsziele für Automobilhersteller, beraten.
Carlo Martuscelli, Francesca Micheletti und Graham Lanktree haben zu diesem Bericht beigetragen.

Live: Jillaroos begin home World Cup against Fetu Samoa
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:33:23 UTC
16:33:23 KST

Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Rugby League World Cup : Australia defeats Fetu Samoa 40-0
Australia's quest for a fourth consecutive Women's Rugby League World Cup has started with a bang courtesy of a 40-0 victory over Fetu Samoa.
Unbackable favourites leading into the tournament opener, the Jillaroos overcame an ill-disciplined opening 10 minutes to shut out Samoa in the seven-try rout.
Things were far from easy for Australia in the second half, but the damage was already done by half-time, with five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher and reigning Dally M medallist Tamika Upton leading the way with two try assists apiece.
Kelleher, making her Jillaroos debut, was named player of the match, where she was dangerous in attack and her kicking game troubled Samoa.
Speaking to ABC Sport, Kelleher said she had been waiting a long time for her chance to play for the Jillaroos.
"It's a dream come true," she said.
"Was in the squad last year, but got my debut jersey this year. So excited and so happy to be here."
Despite the 40-point win, it was far from a perfect performance from the reigning world champions.
"We still have a lot of things to fix from today. It wasn't perfect out there," Kelleher said.
Samoa, in their first World Cup since 2008, had several chances early but lacked the class to capitalise against their much-fancied opponents.
Gold Coast Titans star Jaime Chapman ended her three-year Jillaroos exodus by scoring Australia's first try in the 11th minute, beating opposite winger Freedom Crichton Ropati out wide.
Australia's greatest ever try-scorer, Julia Robinson, lived up to her reputation seven minutes later when she beat three would-be defenders for her 23rd Jillaroos try in 14 appearances.
Tries to back-rower Shaylee Bent and hooker Keeley Nizza followed in quick succession before lock Olivia Kernick crossed moments before halftime to seal a 28-0 lead at the break.
Kernick turned playmaker in the opening five minutes of the second period when she handed the ball off for Keilee Joseph to extend the Jillaroos' lead.
Brave defence might have turned the tide for Samoa, who ground their way to more opportunities at the Jillaroos end over the final 25 minutes.
Prop Laikha Clarke went the closest to securing some consolation points for Samoa, but was ruled to have dropped the ball over the line.
Of further concern for Samoa was a suspected knee injury in the dying stages to centre Sarina Masaga.
A try in the final two minutes from Australian centre Jessica Sergis capped the Jillaroos' victory and extended their almost three-year unbeaten run.
Samoa's men thrashed France in the opening match of the day, putting on a record score to win 78-4.

REPORT: Samoa 78 def. France 4
— reporting by AAP
Samoa have opened their World Cup campaign by crushing France in a 78-4 win that gives an early boost to the Pacific nation's hopes of reaching the knockout stages.
In a 14-try-to-one victory in which centre Stephen Crichton kicked 11 goals and Melbourne flyer Sua Fa'alogo crossed four times, the Samoans barely worked up a sweat at Western Sydney Stadium in Sydney on Friday.
Taking on a French side mostly made up of Super League players, the star-studded Samoan team raced out to a 28-0 lead inside 20 minutes.
The only blemish for coach Ben Gardiner was the sight of Brisbane winger Deine Mariner going off in the first half with a suspected injury.
And while they had lapses of discipline and concentration with the result sewn up — France scored their sole try through winger Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet — the heavy win will increase Samoa's points differential and their hopes of making it to the semi-finals.
One of Samoa, England or Tonga will miss the knockout stages as a result of the new tournament format, in which the top two teams from across group B and group C make it to the last four.
Samoa face Papua New Guinea in Port Moresby next week before concluding their pool games in an all-Pacific match-up for the ages against the Tongans.
The Kumuls on home soil and Tonga in Sydney will provide a much sterner test than the French, who were left for dead in a blistering opening quarter.
Mariner scored the opening try for the Toa in the third minute soon after his father Lapi had sung the country's national anthem that brought stars including Jarome Luai and Spencer Leniu to tears.
Benaiah Ioelu, Jermaine McEwen, Fa'alogo, and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow all crossed in the next 15 minutes as the French defence was cut to shreds.
Aispuro-Bichet briefly stemmed the bleeding before Fa'alogo went in again just before halftime to make it 34-4 at the break.
The French had little resistance in the second period, with Fa'alogo adding two more while Crichton, Chanel Harris-Tavita, Shawn Blore, Izack Tago, Francis Molo and Ioelu all went over.

Syria arrests 'Butcher of Baniyas' accused of 2013 coastal massacres
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:33:01 UTC
16:33:01 KST

Ali Kayali, 70, known as Mihrac Ural, commanded al-Assad-affiliated militia forces that carried out summary executions of more than 450 civilians in Bayda and Baniyas in May 2013.
Syria's General Intelligence Directorate has arrested Ali Kayali, the al-Assad era militia commander linked to the 2013 Bayda and Baniyas massacres, as he attempted to flee the country, state-run SANA news agency reported.
Known by his alias Mihrac Ural, Kayali is accused of commanding armed groups that carried out killings alongside forces of ousted dictator Bashar al-Assad, including in the coastal province of Tartus, and in rural areas of Latakia, Aleppo and Idlib.
The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights cited unnamed sources who said Kayali was taken from his home in the Mansourieh area of Lebanon, not at a Syrian border crossing.
According to those sources, armed men with Lebanese accents entered the property, apprehended Kayali's wife and brother-in-law, and removed him from the premises. Lebanese authorities have not commented on this report.
Kayali, 70, has been linked to the killings in Bayda and Baniyas in May 2013, when regime forces and allied militias stormed residential areas in Tartus province and carried out summary executions of civilians.
The Syrian Network for Human Rights documented 264 deaths in Bayda, including 36 children and 28 women, and 195 in Ras al-Nabeh, including 56 children and 43 women.
A Human Rights Watch report published in September 2013 documented at least 248 deaths across the two locations, noting the real figure was likely higher.
Witness accounts described bodies left in streets, shops and basements, executions carried out with firearms and bladed weapons, and homes set alight alongside the dead.
Who is Ali Kayali?
Born in the Turkish city of Antakya in 1956, Kayali was active in armed organisations including the Popular Salvation Front in Turkey and the Front for the Liberation of the Iskenderun Brigade, both designated terrorist organisations by Ankara.
He fled to Syria in 1982, obtained Syrian citizenship and changed his name. He reportedly cultivated close ties to the al-Assad family through his wife.
When the Syrian civil war began in 2011, he took command of the Popular Front for the Liberation of the Iskenderun Brigade, which fought alongside regime forces, primarily along Syria's coast.
Kayali's detention follows that of Jamal Trabelsi, described in reports as his deputy, who was arrested by Syria's Internal Security Forces on 4 October.
Turkish authorities announced the separate arrest of Omar al-Khatib earlier this month as he attempted to reach Europe by sea. Media reports describe him as one of the planners of the Reyhanli bombing and say he coordinated with members of al-Assad-era intelligence services.
Syria's Interior Ministry has said it is continuing to pursue individuals accused of involvement in abuses under the former regime as part of efforts to achieve transitional justice.
Damascus has stepped up efforts to restore trust in Syria's government and its services following a 13-year-long war in the country that resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands and saw millions displaced and seeking refuge outside the country.
Trust in authorities in neighbouring Lebanon is among the lowest in the world, with 56% of Lebanese citizens believing the government does not care about them at all, about double the global figure (29%), according to the latest research by Gallup for Lloyd's Register Foundation's World Risk Poll.

Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
10:15:02 EEST
16:15:02 KST

The National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine and the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office have served notices of suspicion to forensic experts of the Kyiv Research Institute of Forensic Expertise (KRIFE) of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine who drew up deliberately false conclusions regarding the value of elite real estate belonging to the wife of a high-ranking Security Service of Ukraine official.
"In December 2023, the wife of the high-ranking official purchased an apartment for UAH 21.6 million. At the same time, according to the contract, its value was intentionally understated to UAH 12.8 million. In April 2024, a lawyer acting in the interests of the couple initiated a forensic construction and technical examination at KRIFE. Already in May, a commission of experts issued a conclusion stating that the market value of this apartment is UAH 12.3 million, which is UAH 9.3 million lower than the actual price. To achieve this result, the experts intentionally used non-relevant real estate objects for comparison. Subsequently, this document was used by the defense as evidence in the NACP, NABU, and court," the NABU press service reported on its Telegram channel.
In the same month, NABU detectives, investigating criminal proceedings into the apartment's purchase, ordered a commission examination, which was recalled on November 11, 2024, with a request to return the materials without execution.
"However, the experts ignored the investigative demand and continued their research. They agreed on limiting the value of comparison objects to no higher than $2,500–2,600 per square meter (instead of the market $3,000) and consciously chose the cheapest offers starting from $1,550, while ignoring other available analogues. In early December 2024, the experts signed the conclusion but backdated it to November 8, 2024 (i.e., prior to the recall by the NABU detective). Significantly, detectives received a copy of the conclusion not from KRIFE, but from the lawyer of the suspected high-ranking official," the report notes.
NABU emphasizes that such manipulations of evidence would be impossible if an independent expert institution operated under the Bureau.
"The Bureau's leadership has for several years emphasized the critical need to create an independent expert institution. This would eliminate corruption risks, prevent external pressure on experts, and significantly increase the efficiency of pre-trial investigations in top corruption cases," NABU summarized.

Why is Switzerland voting again on the ‘marriage tax penalty’?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
07:00:00 UTC
16:00:00 KST

Why is Switzerland voting again on the ‘marriage tax penalty’?
On November 29, the Swiss will vote for the second time this year on how to end the tax disadvantage faced by married couples. After saying yes to individual taxation in March, voters must now decide on the Fair Taxation Initiative submitted by the Centre Party, which wants to keep joint taxation.
It is not the first time that the Swiss have voted more than once on the same issue. The Covid-19 Act was put to the electorate three times in as many years. This time, the Swiss will vote on November 29 on an alternative way of ending the marriage tax penalty – although they accepted the principle of individual taxation just a few months ago.
Why hold another vote on the taxation of married couples?
At present, married couples are taxed jointly. Their incomes are added together to calculate their tax due. For some spouses, this results in a higher tax bill than if they were unmarried. This is particularly the case when both spouses have a high income. It is known as the “marriage tax penalty”.
To put an end to this disparity, on March 8 Swiss voters approved the Individual Taxation Act. This was an indirect counter-proposal by the government to a popular initiative launched by the women’s wing of the centre-right Radical-Liberal Party. The reform is supposed to take effect in 2032. From then on, each taxpayer will be taxed based on their own tax return, at federal, cantonal and municipal levels alike.
The Centre Party, however, is not in favour of this principle. It decided to press ahead with its own popular initiativeExternal link, which proposes a different way of ending the tax discrimination faced by some married couples. The text, entitled “Yes to fair federal taxes for married couples – to finally put an end to marriage-based discrimination!”, was submitted to the Federal Chancellery on March 27, 2024, accompanied by 102,051 valid signatures.
What does the Centre Party’s initiative entail?
The initiative calls for the joint taxation of married couples to be maintained, but only for direct federal tax. This means that the spouses’ incomes would be added together and the couple would file a joint tax return. The text also stipulates that married couples should not pay more tax than unmarried people in a comparable financial situation. This principle would be enshrined in the Constitution.
The initiative does not set out the exact calculation method, but tasks the legislature with finding a solution. It does, however, provide for a fallback mechanism if no implementing legislation comes into force within three years of its adoption. In that case, the tax authorities would have to carry out two calculations: one based on joint taxation and the other using the tax scales and deductions applicable to unmarried individuals. The lower of the two amounts would then be taken into account.
Who is for and who against?
A cross-party committee supports the initiative. It comprises the Centre Party, the right-wing Swiss People’s Party, the Evangelical Party, the ultra-conservative Federal Democratic Union, as well as the Swiss Farmers’ Union and the “Famille 3plus” interest group. The federal government and parliament recommend rejecting the proposal. The left-wing Social Democratic Party, the Green Party, the Radical-Liberals and the Liberal Greens are also against.
What are the arguments in favour of the initiative?
The proponents regard it as the fairest solution to end the tax penalty on marriage. They argue that individual taxation disadvantages families in which one parent provides the bulk of the income, while the other earns little or nothing at all. Their model, they say, allows couples to decide for themselves how to divide paid work and family responsibilities, without being penalised fiscally for this choice.
They also stress that the initiative does not require a complete overhaul of the tax system, as it builds on the existing joint taxation model. This, they argue, would preclude the additional administrative burden linked to individual taxation, which would generate some 1.7 million extra tax returns, according to government estimates.
Lastly, the initiative’s proponents highlight the situation of retired couples who have organised their lives for decades on the basis of joint taxation. A change in system could put them at a disadvantage, as they can no longer adapt the division of labour and income that prevailed during their working lives.
And the arguments against?
The opponents argue that the goal of ending the tax penalty on marriage was already achieved with the approval of individual taxation last March. They therefore call for this democratic decision to be respected.
The critics also point out that, in certain situations, the initiative could create a new form of inequality, this time to the detriment of unmarried people. They could end up paying more tax than married couples in a comparable financial situation.
Furthermore, the adoption of the proposal would create a situation at odds with the principle of taxing each taxpayer individually. As the Centre’s initiative concerns only direct federal tax, it could give rise to a dual system: married couples would be taxed jointly at federal level, but individually at cantonal and municipal levels.
Lastly, according to the opponents, joint taxation provides less of an incentive to engage in gainful employment than individual taxation, particularly for the person bringing in the household’s second income. They therefore believe that the initiative does less to promote equality between women and men.
What about the fiscal cost of this reform?
The financial implications of the initiative would depend on how it is implemented. If the proposed alternative method of calculation were applied, it would result in an estimated reduction in direct federal tax revenue of between CHF700 million ($842 million) and CHF1.4 billion per year, according to the federal government’s dispatch to parliamentExternal link. By way of comparison, the individual taxation system approved in March is expected to result in a shortfall of around CHF630 million per year in direct federal tax revenue.
Will individual taxation be scrapped if the initiative is accepted?
Not necessarily. Even if the Centre’s initiative is accepted on November 29, the law on individual taxation, approved by the electorate in March, will remain in force. The federal government has set its implementation for 2032.
However, acceptance of the initiative would give rise to a contradictory situation. The Constitution would enshrine the joint taxation of married couples for direct federal tax, whereas the law would require a shift to individual taxation. It would then be up to parliament to resolve this contradiction.

According to updated data, the Russians carried out 83 airstrikes yesterday, using 271 guided bombs. The invaders also deployed 7,059 kamikaze drones and fired on populated areas and Defense Forces positions 2,551 times, including 76 times using multiple-launch rocket systems.

The Russian Federation carried out an airstrike on Vilna Sloboda.
Over the past day, Ukrainian aviation struck an area where Russian troops were concentrated.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk directions, the invaders dropped three guided aerial bombs over the past day and fired on the positions of the Defense Forces and populated areas 64 times.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna direction, Ukrainian defenders repelled 22 enemy attacks. The Russians attempted to attack in the areas of Starytsia, Izbytske, and Chuhunivka, toward Buzove and Radkivka.
In the Kupiansk sector, the Russian army attempted three times to improve its positions, conducting assault operations toward Novoosynove and Shyikivka.
In the Lyman sector, Russian troops launched eight attacks toward Novoyehorivka, Olhivka, Druzhlyubivka, Lyman, and Stary Karavan. Their attempts to breach Ukrainian defenses were repelled.
In the Sloviansk sector, the invaders launched two attacks toward Orikhuvatka and Mykolaivka.
In the Kramatorsk sector, Ukrainian defenders halted three enemy attempts to advance in the Chervonyi area and toward Yurkivka.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, the Russians carried out 27 attacks: they conducted offensive operations in the Kostiantynivka and Dovha Balka areas, toward Rozkishne, Mykolaipillia, and Raiske.
In the Pokrovsk sector, the invaders attacked 60 times: they attempted to advance in the areas of Dorozhne and Molodetske, toward Toretsk, Pavlivka, Novopavlivka, Vilne, Kucherevy Yar, Hannivka, Dobropillia, Svitle, Krasnopodillia, Serhiivka, and Muravka.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, Russian forces did not carry out any assault operations.
In the Huliaipole sector, the Russian army attacked Ukrainian defenders’ positions 20 times, attempting to advance toward Rizdvyanka, Dolynka, Hirkyi, and Yehorivka.
In the Orikhiv sector, the invaders attempted to attack toward Pavlivka twice.
In the Dnipro River sector, Russian forces did not carry out any assault operations.
In the Volyn and Polissia sectors, no signs of the enemy forming offensive groups were detected.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russia lost 1,790 of its soldiers in the war against Ukraine over the past 24 hours.

Fed chair reaffirms price stability commitment, avoids signaling next rate move
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
06:57:45 UTC
15:57:45 KST

Mucahithan Avcioglu
16 October 2026•Update: 16 October 2026
US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reaffirmed the central bank's commitment to price stability Friday while declining to signal policy decisions at its remaining meetings this year.
Speaking with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Warsh said the Fed had withdrawn some monetary accommodation about a month earlier.
He said developments since the September meeting had broadly conformed to expectations, adding that policymakers would assess output, employment, and inflation when making decisions in October and December.
Warsh declined to prejudge those meetings, describing his approach as part of a new chapter at the Fed.
 
Investment surge supports economic resilience
Warsh said the US is experiencing a substantial investment surge, contrasting current structural growth with earlier concerns about prolonged economic stagnation.
He attributed the investment expansion to sound macroeconomic policies and strong microeconomic foundations, calling it one of the most significant positive developments in the global economy.
The surge is broadening beyond artificial intelligence, providing strength and durability to the US economy, although that momentum is not shared everywhere, he added.
Warsh said global economic resilience had exceeded what he would have anticipated five or six months earlier, given geopolitical tensions.
However, inflation remained a common challenge. He said central banks had undertaken broadly synchronized monetary tightening in recent months, with his counterparts showing determination to restore price stability.
 
AI could reshape monetary policymaking
Warsh described AI as potentially the most consequential economic transformation of his lifetime, saying it was boosting demand before its supply-side benefits materialized.
He said he expected the technology to deliver a positive supply shock over the medium term, raising productivity and wealth, while cautioning that the transition could be uneven.
Its employment effects over the next 12-18 months remained uncertain, alongside questions about which companies would profit from the technology.
AI could also fundamentally change monetary policymaking by helping central banks analyze information and distinguish underlying economic trends from delayed or noisy data, he said.
Warsh said a Fed task force on productivity and jobs would hold its first field hearing on Nov. 16 in San Francisco’s Bay Area to examine these issues.

Berlin and Paris open ‘Made in Europe’ door to Switzerland
Germany and France are opening the door for Switzerland to join the ‘Made in Europe’ industrial policy, subject to strict conditions.
Switzerland would be treated on an equal footing with the countries of the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom.
This is according to a Franco-German position paper published on Thursday, a copy of which has been seen by the Keystone-SDA news agency. Not all German political parties have approved the proposal to include Switzerland, cautioned a diplomat in Brussels speaking on condition of anonymity.
The French news agency AFP was the first to report on this development.
Switzerland’s participation would be subject to conditions and would require formal association, the diplomat explained.
The term “Made in Europe” refers to a European preference in public procurement, which the EU is currently discussing. It is a matter of debate whether non-EU European states such as Switzerland should be included in this or not.
The Swiss government has been lobbying its European neighbours on this issue for months.

The spectre of far-right leader Marine Le Pen winning France’s presidency with a pledge to go head-to-head with the European Union is already giving Brussels the jitters -- and looming large over Emmanuel Macron’s final months in power.
France heads to the polls in April and May, after which Macron will exit as he can only serve two terms as president of the EU’s second-largest economy.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
But as Macron met his EU counterparts for a Brussels summit, a European diplomat said Le Pen was already “in the room” -- with the frontrunner’s potential victory hanging over their talks Thursday and Friday on future spending and Ukraine.
Seeking to tighten the screws on the EU, Le Pen travelled to the Belgian capital on the eve of the leaders’ meeting to address the media, vowing to slash France’s contribution to the European Union budget and to cut short financial support to Ukraine.
European officials do not hide their concerns that Le Pen is trying to exert influence over EU affairs months before the vote.
“It was very cunning of her to hold her press conference” the day before, said a second European diplomat, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The National Rally leader also spoke at length to the Financial Times newspaper, read by policymakers in Brussels, warning of a potential showdown over the EU budget and difficult times for EU chief Ursula von der Leyen if she wins.
Macron Says Ukraine Must Have ‘All Means’ to Defend Itself, Pledges New Aviation Aid
The interview was “quite scary” especially on Ukraine, said Francesco Nicoli, politics professor at Italy’s Polytechnic University of Turin.
A senior European official admitted Brussels could barely imagine what the EU would look like with a French far-right government -- with no known formal contacts between Le Pen and the EU executive to date.
- ‘Possible storm’ -
For Macron, fears of a disruptive Le Pen presidency have sharpened focus on what he may yet achieve at EU level in his final few months in power.
The fervent European who has spent nine years pushing deeper EU integration maintains influence over his counterparts in Brussels, diplomats say, despite a pileup of crises at home from student protests to French debt turmoil.
“What is certain is that in Brussels there is the will to make the most of the fact he is still there, and to lock in whatever can be before a possible storm,” said Sebastien Maillard, of the Jacques Delors Institute.
Observers note that no other current EU leader has managed to take on a leadership role in the bloc, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz weaker than ever after the strongest far-right win in Germany since 1945.
“Macron understands what is happening around the (leaders’) table. He’s a very skilled negotiator and much more agile than Merz,” the first EU diplomat said.
EU watchers say Macron will need all his savvy to prevail in the fraught negotiations over the budget between the so-called “frugals” led by Berlin and capitals like Paris seeking a more ambitious budget.
Maillard said the French president had “acquired an international reputation” which could “to a certain extent, protect him from France’s domestic difficulties”.
The expert pointed to Macron’s influence over talks on Christine Lagarde’s successor as head of the European Central Bank and the EU budget talks.
Not everyone is convinced.
“On foreign and security policy, Macron is in a strong position right now. On economic issues he’s weak,” academic Nicoli said.
The French leader himself, perhaps wanting to avoid Le Pen further overshadowing his summit talks, did not take any questions from journalists in Brussels Thursday.
“I think that’s why Macron is keeping a low profile. He doesn’t want to respond,” a diplomatic source said.

Pornography showing strangulation and incest to be banned in UK from early November
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-16
06:52:54 UTC
15:52:54 KST

Pornography that depicts strangulation and incestuous relationships will be banned in England and Wales from early November, the government has announced.
The content will be outlawed from 6 November after cross-party pressure prompted ministers to announce new legislation earlier this year.
Online pornography depicting strangulation or suffocation, sex between people who are related or pretending to be related, or when somebody is pretending to be a child under 16, will be illegal.
The justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said: “This isn’t about criminalising harmless sexual preferences. But porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people.
“Content that normalises, or even glorifies, violence against women is dangerous and can blur the line with what is acceptable in real life.”
The Conservative peer Gabby Bertin made the recommendations in her review into pornography regulation which reported in 2025.
Her report found pornography that shows women being choked can have “devastating” real-world consequences. It highlighted “disturbing” role-play, including incest and adults portraying children. Both will be banned.
The report said there had been a “total absence of government scrutiny” of the pornography industry.
Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence in its own right, but it is not illegal to show it online.
Reacting to the announcement, Lady Bertin said: “It is very good news these offences will come into force, and not a moment too soon.
“This change in law alongside better enforcement and stronger regulation will send the unequivocal signal not only to the companies that host and facilitate porn but also to wider society that extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable.”
The End Violence Against Women Coalition campaign group welcomed the ban, urging ministers to ensure it is enforced.
Its interim director, Janaya Walker, said: “This is an important step towards tackling the normalisation of violence against women and girls, and the result of years of campaigning by EVAW and other experts who have raised concerns about the impact of violent pornography.
“Strangulation can cause serious, lasting harm and even death, yet its widespread portrayal in pornography risks normalising this violence in sexual relationships, particularly among young people.
“The introduction of this offence is an important recognition of the harm caused by violent pornography and the need to hold an industry accountable for content that depicts and profits from violence against women and girls.
“The government must now ensure the ban is effectively enforced, and update the Online Safety Act so that online platforms are required to remove this content.”

Senior Brethren had 'brief' meeting with far-right figures during election
